subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should unconfigured memorySearch.sync.intervalMinutes become a non-zero default fallback, or should periodic memory sync remain opt-in while relying on watcher/search freshness?
rationale: Changing this default can add background filesystem/hash scans and provider work for existing users, while leaving it at 0 may preserve the reported stale-index failure if watcher/search events are missed.

options.title: Default-on fallback after review
options.body: Accept a non-zero periodic fallback once the linked PR or replacement proves upgrade behavior and scopes dirty marking correctly.

options.title: Keep interval opt-in
options.body: Leave the default at 0 and document intervalMinutes as the workaround if maintainers do not want new background sync behavior for existing users.

options.title: Close as watcher-refactor solved
options.body: Close only if maintainers can point to source or live proof that newer watcher/search sync behavior prevents stale memory indexes without a periodic fallback.

recommendation.title: Default-on fallback after review
recommendation.body: Accept a non-zero periodic fallback once the linked PR or replacement proves upgrade behavior and scopes dirty marking correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: The current relevant memory resolver and manager-sync regions are blamed to his recent refactor, making him the best available routing candidate from history.
